solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Creature spinning around on food at party

indicators.note: spinning around turns the joined words back to front, so they are read from the end

parts.note: on means about or concerning, RE
dips are the sauces put out for dunking at a party

explanation.surface: Some creepy-crawly whirls about on the buffet at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning around' turns REDIPS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An arachnid is a living thing, so it counts as a creature in the broad sense.

clue.text: Young fellow with smart clothing is a champion

indicators.note: clothing means the smart word is wrapped around the young fellow like a garment

parts.note: to smart is to hurt, so smart gives PAIN
a lad is a young fellow

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed youth turns out to be a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective about the clothes, but here it is the noun meaning sting, and 'clothing' wraps it round the young fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's knights, hence any heroic defender of a cause.

clue.text: Wild dog finally found place to hide

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word found

parts.note: a hole is somewhere one can hide away

explanation.surface: A wild dog at last found a place to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: The dhole is an Asian wild canine that hunts in packs.

clue.text: Once more performs in problematic scene with art

indicators.note: problematic suggests things gone awry, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An actor does a troublesome scene again, art and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problematic' rearranges SCENE and ART together.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage an event again, acting it out a second time, is the literal sense of the hyphenated verb.

clue.text: Forsaking 19, she and Italian leader get into bed?

indicators.note: forsaking means abandoning, so the letter for the partner from 19 is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
19 refers to the answer at 19-down, a spouse, abbreviated H as in genealogy tables
Il Duce was the title Mussolini took as Italian leader

explanation.surface: A woman leaves her husband and climbs into bed with an Italian chief.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the standard abbreviation for husband. The question mark flags that the definition is a euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone into a sexual encounter is, euphemistically, to get them into bed.

clue.text: Report about millions affected by bad weather

indicators.note: about places the report word round the abbreviation for millions

parts.note: a news report is a story
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A news item on how millions were hit by foul conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempestuous conditions with wind and rain describe a day suffering from bad weather.

clue.text: Dishy sort doctor met abroad

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A handsome person: the doctor one met overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun, a medic, but it is a verb meaning tamper with, rearranging MET ABROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishy person is attractive, the sort one swoons over, the very meaning of this informal word.

clue.text: Deceive guerrilla leader a great deal

parts.note: Che Guevara was the famous guerrilla leader
tons means a lot, so a ton is a great deal

explanation.surface: A rebel commander strikes a huge bargain by trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unfaithful to a partner is to betray or deceive them.

clue.text: Do everything possible to take a trip alone?

definitions.meaning: to be overeager, going to great lengths to help or please
read literally, stumbling over nobody's feet but one's own

explanation.surface: Going all out by travelling solo on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey but is a stumble, and 'alone' means with no one else to trip over.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone so keen they practically stumble in their eagerness to do things.

clue.text: Stop rifles — about five hundred — being deployed for deadly pursuits

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged rifle letters round the Roman numeral
being deployed suggests things spread out into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A plea to halt guns as five hundred are sent into killing activities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being deployed' jumbles STOP RIFLES into FIELSPORTS, and 'about' wraps that round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting, shooting and fishing are the countryside activities that kill their quarry.

clue.text: Self-control shown by soldiers facing defeat, cut off in foreign country

indicators.note: in places the soldiers and the shortened defeat word inside the country

parts.note: France is a foreign country from a British viewpoint
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: cut off removes the final letter of the defeat word

parts.note: to beat is to defeat

explanation.surface: Troops showing restraint after a loss abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' drops the last letter of the defeat word, and 'in' puts both pieces inside the country; 'facing' and 'shown by' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient restraint, holding back from reacting, is a form of self-control.

clue.text: Fellow leads driver out of odd parts

indicators.note: taking the odd-placed letters out of the phrase leaves its even-placed letters

explanation.surface: A man leads a driver away from strange regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like strange, but means the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters, which are thrown out of 'leads driver'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name is a fair answer for a fellow, as names often are in crosswords.

clue.text: Two qualifications available in reform school once

indicators.note: available in signals the pair of degrees found sitting inside the reform word

parts.note: to reform something is to alter it

indicators.note: two means the qualification is used twice

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a qualification

explanation.surface: A reformatory offers two certificates to inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform school' looks like one unit, but 'reform' gives ALTER and 'school once' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a former place of study, the institution one attended in the past.

clue.text: What's principally dangerous at any time, likely to explode?

definitions.text: What's principally dangerous at any time, likely to explode?

indicators.note: principally takes the leading letter of the word dangerous
likely to explode suggests the letters burst apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle about something perilous that might go off at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'likely to explode' rearranges ANY TIME into YNAMITE after D. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blasting explosive is always dangerous and liable to go off, as the full clue says.

clue.text: Here, BBC studios produced a film for broadcast

indicators.note: for broadcast means the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: produced is made, and a film is a thin veil, so made a veil

explanation.surface: A spot where the BBC made a movie for transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but is a thin covering, a veil. 'Here' points to a place.
explanation.definitionFit: This district of west London houses famous BBC recording studios used for sessions and concerts.

clue.text: European law enforcer in a spin about UN attack

indicators.note: about places the turned letters round the word UN
in a spin means turned round, so the joined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a cop is a police officer who enforces law

explanation.surface: A Continental policeman, flustered, attacks the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a spin' turns ECOP into POCE, which goes round UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring suddenly on prey is to attack, as a cat does with a mouse.

clue.text: Outrageous, accommodating old woman in apartment

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the apartment word holds the old woman word

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
gran is an affectionate word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: A shocking scandal: an old lady housed in a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaring, shameless offence is outrageous, the sense in phrases like a blatant breach.

clue.text: Partly suspecting this setter's in a jam

indicators.note: partly indicates only a portion of the word suspecting is used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler suspects they are in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is a gelling agent, and 'jam' is preserve, not a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit compound makes preserves gel, so it is literally what sets jam.

clue.text: I prance about acting the goat?

indicators.note: about means around in a muddle, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to capering around and fooling like a goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I PRANCE. 'Acting the goat' means fooling about, but read literally it is behaving like a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means goatlike, from the Latin for goat, so behaving as one would.

clue.text: Christian who makes weapons

definitions.meaning: ... Christian led the mutiny on HMS Bounty
an arrow-maker, the old trade of a ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks like a believer but is the first name of the Bounty mutineer.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname is the Bounty mutineer's, and the trade word names a craftsman of arrows.

clue.text: Mate is hot on Aerosmith, perhaps

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
Aerosmith is an American rock group, an example of a US band

explanation.surface: A friend is keen on a famous rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is hot on' looks like 'keen on', but 'hot' gives H and 'is ... on' just joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is one's partner in marriage, a life mate.

clue.text: Didn't attend audition for film

indicators.note: audition is hearing, so the word is wanted as it is heard spoken

parts.note: a film is a thin coating, as is a mist on glass

explanation.surface: Someone skipped the casting call for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a casting test but means hearing; 'film' is a haze, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to turn up at an event means one was absent from it.

clue.text: Belching quietly before tucking in? Extremely rude, first and foremost

indicators.note: first and foremost puts the ends of rude at the very front
before puts the soft sign ahead of the tucking-in word
extremely takes the letters at both ends of the word rude

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
to tuck in is to start eating heartily

explanation.surface: Burping softly before diving into a meal: very rude, above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely rude' gives RE, which 'first and foremost' moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is said to keep coming back up when it causes burps, an old sense of this word.

clue.text: Early sign of repentance by youngster, following a crime

indicators.note: following means the other pieces come after the a
early sign of takes the opening letter of repentance

parts.note: a son is a youngster

explanation.surface: A boy's first hint of remorse after committing an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the youngster did it, but the 'crime' is defined on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a serious criminal offence.

clue.text: Grassy area cut after a match

indicators.note: after puts the shortened grass word behind the a
cut docks the final letter of the grassy word

parts.note: a green is a grassy area, as in a village green

explanation.surface: A lawn is mown following a sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a game, but it is the verb meaning correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that match are in accord, the sense of tally or concur.

clue.text: Flight, last arranged between Paris, possibly, and Ireland: luggage is extra

indicators.note: between means the rearranged last sits between the city letters and Ireland
possibly suggests a version of the city name, its letters rearranged
arranged means the letters of last are put into a new order

parts.note: a case is a piece of luggage

explanation.surface: A flight from Paris to Ireland where luggage costs extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' looks like air travel but means a set of steps. 'possibly' gives SPIRA from PARIS; 'arranged' gives LSTA from LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a set of steps, and this one winds round a central post.

clue.text: Story of cricket side's demise

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs
demise is death, an end

explanation.surface: The tale of a cricket team's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is one half of the field, not a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional tale handed down, often fanciful, is a type of story.

clue.text: You and I wear man's garments

indicators.note: wear puts the pronoun for you and I within the man's name, as if in his clothes

parts.note: Ted is a man's name, with the possessive giving TEDS
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: We put on a fellow's clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Suits made from rough woollen cloth are clothes, worn in the country.
